page_title: How to build a simple actor-based blockchain

summary.title: How to build a simple actor-based blockchain
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a toy proof-of-work blockchain in Scala using Akka actors (Broker, Miner, Blockchain and Node), with persistence and a SHA-256 hash puzzle.
takeaways: A blockchain can be modeled as transactions, a linked chain of blocks, and a proof-of-work function that finds a hash with leading zeros.
Scala case classes and sealed traits can represent transactions and chain blocks, with a genesis EmptyChain object.
Akka actors split the node into Broker (pending transactions), Miner (ready/busy states via become), and Blockchain (PersistentActor storing events and snapshots).
The Node actor supervises the other actors and exposes the REST API for sending transactions and mining blocks.
summary.summary: The author walks through Scalachain, a simplified Bitcoin-style blockchain prototype written in Scala with Akka. The article first gives a short conceptual overview of distributed ledgers, proof of work, and forks, then defines the model: transactions, a chain of blocks hashed with SHA-256, a PoW puzzle requiring four leading zeros, and a Node exposing a REST API. The implementation section shows code for case classes, the Chain trait with a custom :: operator, a tail-recursive proof-of-work function, and then explains the actor model before building the Broker, Miner (with ready and busy states), Blockchain (a PersistentActor with events and snapshots), and Node actors. The article is incomplete in the captured text, ending mid-description of the Node actor.
